analysis.one_liner: Hitachi Energy India (formerly ABB Power Products and Systems India) makes power transmission and distribution equipment — transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems and grid automation — for utilities, industry, data centres and renewable energy projects in India.
analysis.whats_happening: Q1 FY27 (June-quarter) results, released in August 2026, showed revenue up 68.6% YoY to ₹2,494cr and PAT up 123.5% to ₹294cr, with operating EBITDA margin at 16.0% and a record order backlog of ₹32,222cr; the stock jumped over 11% on the print. Q2 FY27 (September-quarter) results are due in the first half of November 2026 going by last year's reporting pattern (Q2 FY26 was announced November 3, 2025) — not yet out as of today.
analysis.plain_terms: This business sells the equipment utilities and industry need to move electricity around — transformers, switchgear, HVDC links — and demand is booming as India builds grid capacity for renewables and data centres. The profit growth numbers look dramatic (up 123% in one quarter, up over 400% in another) but a lot of that is recovery from a weak year-ago base when rising input costs squeezed margins; the more honest number is the operating margin, which climbed from about 8% to 16% over the past five quarters. The tension: the stock already prices in years of this growth, trading near 110-120 times earnings, so strong results do not automatically mean a rising share price — the stock is down 25% from its May 2026 peak even as the underlying business kept growing.
analysis.quarters: FY26 was a margin-recovery and order-momentum story: Q2 FY26 revenue +23.3%, margin recovered to 15.2% from 8.1% a year earlier (PAT rose 4x, mostly base effect off a weak ₹52cr prior-year quarter); Q3 FY26 revenue +29.6%, PAT +90.3%, margin 15.6%; Q4 FY26 revenue +46.2%, PAT +79.7%, margin 16.4%. Full FY26: revenue ₹8,148cr (+27.6%), PAT ₹988cr (+157%). That carried into Q1 FY27 (June 2026): revenue +68.6% to ₹2,494cr, PAT +123.5% to ₹294cr, margin 16.0%, backlog at a record ₹32,222cr. Management flagged data centres and grid investment as the biggest growth drivers through 2027-28. Treat the headline YoY percentages with caution — several quarters are compared against a weak prior-year margin base; the steady climb in margin (8%→16%) is the more durable signal than the PAT growth rates themselves.
analysis.performance_read: Returns since the March 2020 listing have been extraordinary: 1,031% over 5 years and 533% over 3 years, dwarfing the Nifty (25% and 18%) and peer ABB India (289% and 78%). There is no corporate action (no splits or demergers) distorting this series, so the raw price return is the real return. But the stock is down 25.1% from its May 2026 peak of roughly ₹38,436, and 3-month returns are -11.3% versus the Nifty's -4.9% — a valuation correction after an exceptional run, not evidence of a business problem.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades at roughly 110-120x trailing earnings and about 25x book value (one aggregator cited a much higher P/E near 211x, but that looks stale or miscalculated against the clustered screener-based sources and is set aside). Why it's expensive: the market is pricing in several more years of 20-30%+ order and earnings growth tied to India's grid and data-centre capex cycle, backed by ROCE near 29% and ROE around 21%. Whether that is cheap or expensive depends entirely on whether this growth rate and margin level can be sustained for years — not on whether the business is good today.
analysis.growth_read: Growth has been both volume-led and margin-led over the past year — the order backlog has roughly doubled from pre-FY26 levels to a record ₹32,222cr, while operating EBITDA margin has expanded from roughly 8% to 16% as input-cost pressure eased and the company executed higher-value HVDC and grid-automation orders. That combination of rising volumes and rising margin is more durable than a margin-only story, but a 16% margin is still being tested against the same copper/silver cost swings that have squeezed comparable players.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting into a strong balance sheet — the company is almost debt-free (debt-to-equity ~0.02) with cash of roughly ₹2,672cr, and working capital is negative (around -46 days), meaning it collects from customers faster than it pays suppliers; receivable days improved from ~89 to ~78. Free cash flow figures found across sources were inconsistent (one source cites ~₹203cr for FY26, another cites a very different ~₹1,366cr for the prior year) and could not be reconciled — not verified, check the company's own cash flow statement directly. The dominant risk here is business/valuation risk — whether this growth rate persists at this price — not financial risk.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is Hitachi Energy Ltd, wholly owned by Hitachi Ltd of Japan, holding 71.31% as of September 2026 — down from 75% as of December 2024/March 2025, a one-time stake dilution rather than ongoing selling, since the level has held flat for several quarters since. No promoter pledging was found in available sources, consistent with a foreign-parent-owned entity. FII holding has been rising (toward ~12%), while domestic mutual fund holding has been trimmed in recent quarters (from ~4.3% to ~3.5% by June 2026) — no marquee Indian retail investor name appears on the register.
strengths: Record order backlog of ₹32,222.1cr as of June 2026, up from ₹29,555cr in March 2026 — multi-year revenue visibility
Operating EBITDA margin expanded from 8.1% (Q2 FY25) to 16.0% (Q1 FY27)
Near debt-free balance sheet with debt-to-equity of ~0.02 and negative working capital days
ROCE of ~29% and ROE of ~21%, well above the cost of capital
watchpoints: Valuation at ~110-120x earnings leaves little room for a growth disappointment — stock is already down 25% from its May 2026 peak
Headline YoY profit growth (100%+ in several quarters) partly reflects recovery from a weak margin base in FY25, not purely new demand

Input costs (copper, silver) have squeezed margins at comparable players (e.g. ABB India's margin fell from 13.6% to 12.6% in its latest quarter) — a risk to watch even though this company's own margin has so far held up
Dividend yield is negligible (0.03%) despite a rising per-share payout, because the share price has risen far faster than the dividend
analysis.one_thing: Whether the order backlog converts into revenue at a sustained operating margin near 16% over the next 2-3 quarters — a slip in either execution or margin would directly challenge the 100x+ earnings multiple the market is currently paying.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly results (Q1 FY27 through full FY26) and order-backlog figures were cross-checked across Hitachi Energy press releases, Business Standard, Univest and ICICI Direct and were consistent. Valuation multiples cluster around P/E 108-120x on screener-based sources; one aggregator cited P/E ~211x, which looks stale or miscalculated and was set aside as the outlier. Free cash flow figures conflicted across two sources (~₹203cr vs ~₹1,366cr) and could not be reconciled — check the company's own cash flow statement before quoting a number. Promoter pledge status could not be positively confirmed either way; none was reported in searches. Note: POWERINDIA (Hitachi Energy India) is a separate listed company from ABB India Ltd (ticker ABB) — both trace back to the same original ABB India entity and are frequently conflated by aggregator pages; care was taken to use only Hitachi Energy India / POWERINDIA-specific figures.
